t.4.63.1: Informed by the king of vultures, the monkeys, valiant as lions, leapt up together and, filled with joy, roared aloud.
t.4.63.2: Having heard Sampāti's words about Rāvaṇa's dwelling, the monkeys, delighted and longing to see Sītā, came to the ocean.
t.4.63.3: Having approached that region, those of fearsome valour beheld it standing there like a complete reflection of the vast world.
t.4.63.4: Having reached the northern shore of the southern ocean, the foremost of the monkeys, all together, then made their encampment there.
t.4.63.5: It was teeming with huge and grotesque creatures of many kinds sporting in the water, with gaping mouths and enormous bodies, and it was agitated by waves.
t.4.63.6: In one place it seemed as if asleep, and elsewhere as if at play, and here and there it was covered with masses of water as large as mountains.
t.4.63.7: Seeing that hair-raising sight, teeming with lords of the Dānavas who dwell in the depths of Pātāla, the elephants among monkeys lost heart.
t.4.63.8: Seeing the ocean, as hard to cross as the sky, all the monkeys were suddenly overcome with despair and said, "How is this to be done?"
t.4.63.9: Seeing the army despondent from gazing upon the ocean, the best of monkeys comforted the monkeys, who were stricken with fear.
t.4.63.10: We have no use for sinking down in dejection; despondency is the greater fault. Despondency destroys a man as an angry serpent kills a child.
t.4.63.11: This despondency overpowers a man when the moment for valour has arrived; and for one who is bereft of vigour, the aim of man is not accomplished.
t.4.63.12: When that night had passed, Aṅgada, together with the vānaras, met with the elders among the monkeys and once again held counsel.
t.4.63.13: That army of the monkeys, having surrounded Aṅgada, shone like the host of the Maruts standing around Vāsava.
t.4.63.14: Who else would be able to hold back that army of monkeys, apart from the son of Vālin and apart from Hanumān?
t.4.63.15: Then the glorious Aṅgada, subduer of foes, having honoured those elder monkeys and that army, spoke words full of meaning.
t.4.63.16: Who of great might will now leap across the ocean? Who will make Sugrīva, the subduer of foes, true to his promise?
t.4.63.17: O monkeys, what hero could leap across a hundred yojanas? And who could free all these troop-leaders from this great danger?
t.4.63.18: By whose grace might we, having returned from here with our purpose accomplished and happy, behold our wives, our sons, and our homes?
t.4.63.19: By whose grace might we joyfully go back to Rāma and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, and to the mighty Sugrīva?
t.4.63.20: If any monkey among you is able to leap across the ocean, let him quickly grant us here the sacred gift of freedom from fear.
t.4.63.21: Having heard Aṅgada's words, no one said anything at all; that entire army of monkeys there became as if motionless.
t.4.63.22: Once again Aṅgada, the best of monkeys, spoke to those monkeys: "All of you are the foremost among the mighty, firm in your valor."
t.4.63.23: You are born of a distinguished family and have been honoured again and again; indeed, never at any time has there been any hindrance to the going of any one of you.
t.4.63.24: O bulls among the monkeys, tell me what power each of you has for going across.
